cards.prompt: Why is unified memory beneficial for running LLMs locally?
cards.answer: CPU and GPU share the same data without moving it back and forth.

cards.prompt: Order the LLM loading steps on a discrete-GPU system.
items: Load weights from disk into RAM
Transfer weights from RAM to VRAM for inference
Weights stay in VRAM after inference
VRAM freed when model is explicitly unloaded
cards.answer: Disk to RAM, RAM to VRAM, stay in VRAM, freed on explicit unload.

cards.prompt: On unified memory, weights need to be offloaded from RAM to VRAM before inference.
cards.answer: Myth: RAM and VRAM share one pool, so there is no offload step.

cards.prompt: Which is NOT a reason people use Macs for local LLMs?
options: More portable and cheaper for equal performance
cards.answer: Macs lack CUDA; that is an Nvidia feature.

cards.prompt: After inference finishes, model weights stay in VRAM until the model is explicitly ____.
Your GPU's VRAM is full while running an LLM and memory spikes. What can happen?
cards.answer: It can spill into RAM, which is why RAM is still needed for system overhead.
